messages:
aj: Hey — nightly eval flagged a new class of failures on the JSON-output prompt set after the int8 bring-up. Lots of otherwise-correct responses but with unexpected newline tokens inserted inside string fields, which breaks downstream JSON parsing.

aj: Example from run 202403/slot-7 (trimmed):
```
{
  "id": 42,
  "title": "Release notes for v1.2\n",
  "changes": ["fix A", "improve B"]
}
```

aj: Notice the literal `\n` inside the title string — not present in golden. It causes our JSON loader to error. Seen across ~120/10k samples (1.2%), spike vs baseline 0.03%.

lee: Ugh. Is the token actually `\n` or is it a real newline injected mid-string?

aj: It's the literal backslash+n sequence in the tokenization sequence, not a linebreak. If you paste the model output into a parser it fails.

nightly-eval-bot: [metric] json_parse_fail_rate: baseline=0.0003 -> current=0.012 (p95 regressed) | trace: https://ci.redwood/evals/202403/1739951234

sarah: Any correlation with sequence length / EOS placement? Could be a KV cache alignment/quant rounding artifact.

aj: Quick stats: skewed to prompts where title contains abbreviations and punctuation. Higher at longer contexts (>512 tokens). No clear region/rack correlation.

alex: Can you paste the prompt and full model token ids for one repro case? I can run a small decode with logits diff.

aj: Pasted minimal repro below. Prompt + expected JSON.
```
PROMPT: 
Generate JSON metadata for the release.
EXPECTED: {"id": 42, "title": "Release notes for v1.2", ...}
MODEL_OUT (tokens): [ 502, 12, 998, 10, 92, 128, 27, 34, "\n", 400, ... ]
```

alex: Hmm token 34 is a backslash, 92 is 'n'? I'll diff logits around those positions. Running `./investigate/decode-diff --model=nightly-int8 --case=1739951234-1` now.

alex: Quick output: prob(backslash) jumps after quantization rounding at step 75; topk becomes noisy and backslash rises to top-1 briefly. Looks like a small spike in logit temperature because of int8 kernel path.

mia: So int8 path changes relative ranking for a low-prob escape char. Could be a kernel precision issue. Any chance it's from the detokenizer merge step?

alex: I checked detokenizer, it's stable. The spike appears in the fused attention kernel output before dequant/rescale.

sarah: Plan: 1) add targeted unit test for JSON prompts; 2) run nightly-eval with float32 runtime on same seed to confirm regression is quant-specific; 3) bisect int8 kernel commits for last week.

aj: I'll add the unit test and a small corpus of failing prompts to the eval set. Pushed branch `aj/json-escape-test`.

nightly-eval-bot: CI job queued: `eval/json-escape-test` (approx 12m).

lee: If it's an int8 kernel bug, we should also toggle fallback-to-fp32 for that op as a quick mitigation for Dedicated customers.

alex: Agree. I can add an opt-in fallback flag and run perf/regression locally. If that fixes the parse-fail rate, we can roll to canary.

mia: Also add a small postprocess sanitizer in the SDK that validates JSON and raises a structured error, so apps don't silently crash. Low friction while kernel fix lands.

aj: Good call. I'll coordinate with SDK to add error type `redwood.parse_error` and include the raw output.

sarah: Assigning: alex -> kernel bisect, aj -> eval + SDK error, mia -> SDK sanitizer PR, lee -> product comms for canary mitigation. Update here when you have results. :thumbsup:

alex: Starting bisect now, will post a short summary when found.

aj: Thanks all — restoring baseline is priority, but good to have both short and long fixes.

alex: Update (10m): bisected to commit `kernel/fuse-attn-20240318` where int8 rescale was tweaked. Re-running that commit with fp32 fallback removes the `\n` spikes in the repro set.

aj: Nice. I'll mark the eval run and notify SRE for canary.

nightly-eval-bot: eval run complete: json_parse_fail_rate -> reduced to 0.0012 on fallback patch branch.

lee: Great. Alex — can you open a PR to revert/tighten the rescale tweak with unit tests?

alex: On it. PR incoming with tests and a flag.

mia: I'll draft SDK sanitizer and error docs after lunch.

sarah: Leaving trace and notes in the incident doc. Good triage, team.

aj: Closing thread when PRs land.
